page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.large is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the compute-optimized c6 instance family. Powered by a KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is backed by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. The resource allocation provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyper-threading, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an L3 cache of 35 MB alongside vector and cryptographic instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), and AES-NI.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures and standard compute execution. Network throughput is bounded by a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default. Given the lack of local NVMe storage, disk-heavy operations will strictly depend on the latency and throughput characteristics of attached block storage volumes.

Benchmark results reflect the constraints of its two-thread, single physical core configuration. In synthetic compute evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1303.98 and a multi-core score of 1735.19, placing it in the lower percentiles across evaluated systems. Geekbench performance follows a similar profile with a single-core score of 1130.0 and a multi-core score of 1355.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers at 12.93 GB/sec for reads and 11.31 GB/sec for writes. Application workloads show modest throughput, including 1.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.93 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, ecs.c6.large offers a low resource footprint suitable for modest computational tasks where larger instances would lead to underutilized capacity. However, the performance density is limited by the single physical core allocation. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, small background workers, build agents, and dev-test environments that do not require high concurrent processing or substantial memory capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, the instance maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory distribution without local storage or GPU hardware. Vector extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and AES are supported at the CPU level. Benchmark evaluations show entry-level throughput consistent with its two-thread capacity, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1355.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2120.23, and static web serving throughput of 1.93 GB/sec. Large-block memory transfers achieve 12.93 GB/sec read and 11.31 GB/sec write bandwidth over a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Due to its limited multi-threaded ceiling and absence of bundled storage, this instance is best matched to light compute tasks, microservices, staging environments, and basic proxy or routing tiers.
